correctness.rationale: Writing the degree-one variables as two outer products gives the projected rank-at-most-two factorization bijectively, and independent central coordinates give exactly q^16. For each full matrix of rank r, count the possible images of the left factor (zero, a line or a plane containing the column space); the column lifts of the right factor have q^{3(2−dim image)} possibilities. This yields the three displayed N values. For rank-one A, row and column operations leave a rank-one block plus a 2×2 block of the form [[0,β],[δ,c−c₀]], so the rank cases and their fields of validity, including characteristic two, follow without genericity. Rank-two A uses the Schur complement, and A=0 gives the listed zero/nonzero cases. The number of rank-one A is (q²−1)²/(q−1); each span has q points. The seven condition counts cover q^8 targets, two with identical qN₂; the other ordered fiber values are distinct by N₀>N₁>N₂>0 and q≥2. Every completed rank-three matrix splits into rank two plus rank one, while the positive zero-fiber stratum rules out width one. The independent outer-product convolution and determinant/minor rank check agreed for all 256 and 6561 targets at q=2 and 3, including 36 and 1152 zero fibers. The proof, not these two replays, covers all prime powers.
residual_risks: The finite corroboration does not sample all prime powers; the central normalization and general field rank argument are exact.
